title: Homework Hotspots
story: Lots of homework is done online now. But many households in Ensley have no internet at home, so kids cannot practice there. Ed Farm works to close the digital skills gap. Libraries, schools and churches could open a free Wi-Fi study spot after school. Your job is to choose where the spots go so that more households with no home internet are within a 10-minute walk of one. Walk times on the map are straight-line estimates.
residentQuote: My kids can't do their homework online at home.

levels.title: Place your first free Wi-Fi study spot
levels.instructions: A function is a button you can press with code. `city.place_hub(...)` puts one free Wi-Fi study spot on the map. Put the name of a place inside the parentheses, in quotes. Place one free Wi-Fi study spot at East Ensley Branch Library. Then press Run and watch the map.
levels.starterCode:
# Level 1: place one free Wi-Fi study spot
# These two lines look at the first place on the list.
places = city.sites()
print(places[0])

# Your turn: call city.place_hub with the name of the place, in quotes.
hints: A function call has a name, then parentheses. What goes inside the parentheses is the thing the function should use. Names of places go in quotes.
Look at the line that starts with `print`. It already calls a function and puts something inside the parentheses. Your line looks the same, but it uses `city.place_hub` instead of `print`.

Here is a different problem. A lunch app has a function called `lunch.add_item`. To add an apple to the tray you would write: lunch.add_item("apple")  The function name comes first and the thing to add goes inside the parentheses, in quotes.

levels.title: Place five free Wi-Fi study spots with a loop
levels.instructions: Writing `city.place_hub` 5 times is slow. A loop does the same job again and again for you. `city.sites()` gives you a list of places. Use a `for` loop to place a free Wi-Fi study spot at the first 5 places on the list. Then press Run.
levels.starterCode:
# Level 2: place 5 free Wi-Fi study spots with a loop
places = city.sites()
print("There are", len(places), "places to choose from.")

# Your turn: use a for loop to place a free Wi-Fi study spot at the first 5 places.
hints: A `for` loop says: do this once for each thing in a list. Which list do you have? What should happen for each place?

A loop starts with `for something in a_list:` and the lines that repeat are indented under it. To use only the first few items of a list, you can cut it with square brackets, like `my_list[:3]`. You want 5.

Here is a different problem. You have a list of pets and want to say hello to the first 3:

pets = ["Milo", "Bean", "Pip", "Rex"]
for pet in pets[:3]:
    print("Hi", pet)

The word after `for` is a name you pick. It stands for one pet each time round the loop.

levels.title: Pick the 5 best places
levels.instructions: The first 5 places on the list are not always the best ones. Each place has `families_nearby`. Here that means households with no internet at home within a 10-minute walk. Sort the places so the biggest number comes first. Then pick 5 free Wi-Fi study spots from the top. One catch: the top places are often right next to each other, and two free Wi-Fi study spots side by side help the same households. Skip a place if both its `lat` and its `lon` are less than 0.01 away from a place you already picked. Then press Run.
levels.starterCode:
# Level 4: sort, then choose
places = city.sites()
chosen = []   # the places you pick will go in here

# Step 1: sort places so the most families_nearby come first.
# Step 2: go down the sorted list. Pick a place unless it is
#         too close to one in chosen. Stop at 5.
# Remember to call city.place_hub for each place you pick.
hints: Do it in two parts. First, put the places in the right order. Then, choose from the top of the list. Try printing the first few sorted places. Where are they on the map?

To sort, use `sorted(list, key=..., reverse=True)`. The `key` tells Python which number to sort by. For each place you look at, ask: is it too close to anyone already in `chosen`? If not, add it to `chosen`.
